sec: Graves eye signs, scoring and diagnosis

items.q: Match the following Graves eye sign to its description — 1) Proptosis 2) Chemosis 3) Diplopia 4) Lid lag … A) Forward displacement of the globe B) Conjunctival oedema C) Restricted extraocular motility D) Lid fails to follow eye on downward gaze
items.exp: Proptosis is forward globe displacement; chemosis is conjunctival oedema; diplopia is from restrictive myopathy and motility restriction; lid lag is failure to follow downward gaze. (Book p911)

items.q: A patient with Graves disease has red, swollen conjunctiva and restricted eye movements bilaterally. The activity score category is most consistent with:
items.exp: Conjunctival redness and oedema with restrictive motility denote active moderate-to-severe Graves ophthalmopathy. (Book p911)

items.q: Assess Graves ophthalmopathy: I Smoking dramatically worsens the course. II Radioiodine therapy can worsen eye disease in active ophthalmopathy.
items.exp: Smoking is the strongest modifiable risk factor for progression; radioiodine can transiently worsen active ophthalmopathy. (Book p911)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — an inactive Graves ophthalmopathy feature?
items.exp: Recent deterioration in diplopia suggests active disease; long-standing proptosis, stable lid lag and fibrotic restrictive strabismus denote inactive disease. (Book p911)

items.q: The single most important modifiable risk factor for progression of Graves ophthalmopathy is ___.
items.exp: Smoking cessation is the strongest modifiable intervention; radioiodine should be avoided or covered with steroids in active disease. (Book p911)

items.q: Match the following Graves investigation to its expected finding — 1) TSH-receptor antibody 2) Anti-TPO 3) Thyroid uptake scan 4) Orbital MRI … A) Positive in most untreated Graves B) Often positive (less specific) C) Diffusely increased uptake D) Enlarged extraocular muscles
items.exp: TRAb is positive in most untreated Graves; anti-TPO is often present but less specific; uptake scan shows diffuse increase; orbital MRI shows enlarged muscle bellies. (Book p911)

items.q: A 40-year-old woman has new thyrotoxicosis, positive TRAb and bilateral proptosis. The most consistent diagnosis is:
items.exp: Positive TRAb with bilateral proptosis and thyrotoxicosis is diagnostic of Graves disease. (Book p911)

items.q: Assess the differential: I Hashitoxicosis can mimic Graves initially. II Toxic adenoma typically has negative TRAb.
items.exp: Hashitoxicosis is a transient Graves-like picture early in Hashimoto disease; toxic adenoma is a focal hot nodule with negative TRAb. (Book p911)

items.q: Match the following clinical clue to the diagnosis — 1) Painful thyroid with elevated ESR 2) Diffuse goitre with bruit 3) Single hot nodule on scan 4) Recent amiodarone use with low uptake … A) Subacute thyroiditis B) Graves disease C) Toxic adenoma D) Type 2 amiodarone thyrotoxicosis
items.exp: Painful thyroid with raised ESR is subacute thyroiditis; diffuse goitre with bruit is Graves; a single hot nodule is toxic adenoma; amiodarone with low uptake is Type 2 destructive thyroiditis. (Book p911)

items.q: An older patient with atrial fibrillation and new weight loss has a thyroid scan with multiple focal hot areas. The best diagnosis is:
items.exp: Multiple focal hot areas in an older patient fit toxic MNG; Graves would be diffusely increased. (Book p911)

items.q: The radioactive iodine uptake pattern in toxic adenoma is ___.
opts: Focally increased in the nodule with suppressed surrounding gland
items.exp: Toxic adenoma shows a focal hot area with suppressed extranodular tissue; toxic MNG shows multiple focal hot areas. (Book p911)

items.q: Assess eye-disease management: I High-dose glucocorticoids are first-line for active moderate-to-severe disease. II Orbital radiotherapy is reserved for active disease failing steroids.
items.exp: IV methylprednisolone is first-line for active moderate-to-severe Graves ophthalmopathy; orbital radiotherapy is an option for active disease not controlled by steroids. (Book p911)
